sources.title: Northern Plains History and Cultures: Belonging
sources.note: Smithsonian Native Knowledge 360 lesson centering Native homelands, kinship, nationhood, governance, and community voices.

sources.title: Oceti Sakowin Essential Understandings and Standards
sources.note: Elder-informed South Dakota standards on Seven Council Fires identity, language divisions, kinship, oral tradition, and chronology cautions.

sources.title: Explore the Seven Council Fires
sources.note: Museum collection overview explaining Dakota, Lakota, and Nakota naming, changing catalog terms, and distinct contemporary nations.

sources.title: Prehistoric Period
sources.note: Minnesota State Archaeologist synthesis of Oneota, Plains Village, Sandy Lake, Psinomani, subsistence, ceramics, and affiliation limits.

sources.title: Jewel Cave Pre-Contact History
sources.note: NPS history describing sparse seasonal evidence and uncertainty about ethnic or linguistic affiliation in the Black Hills.

sources.title: Visiting Sites and Museums
sources.note: State archaeology summaries for Mille Lacs Kathio, Wilford house, wild rice evidence, and ancient pipestone use.

sources.title: Archaeological District in Minnesota Links Past and Present
sources.note: National Park Service account of ancient villages, fish, game, wild rice, waterways, and documented Dakota presence at Mille Lacs in 1679.

sources.title: Sand Lake Archaeological District
sources.note: University archaeology account of an approximately 1500 Oneota site, storage and refuse pits, hearths, foods, tools, and pottery.

sources.title: Village Life
sources.note: University archaeology interpretation of houses, hearths, storage pits, thatch, seasonal groups, and extended-family possibilities.

sources.title: Oneota
sources.note: University overview of Oneota chronology, farming, wild foods, trade, storage pits, and refuse.

sources.title: Oneota Farmers
sources.note: Mississippi Valley Archaeology Center synthesis of Oneota crops, fields, fishing, hunting, gathering, and bison-scapula hoes.

sources.title: Huff Archeological Studies
sources.note: North Dakota history source on a 1443 to 1465 Plains village, houses, plaza, storage, refuse, bison, and trade.

sources.title: Oceti Sakowin Homelands
sources.note: Native-centered stories and place teachings, including corn, medicinal plants, women, children, sacred places, and local scope.

sources.title: Oceti Sakowin Kinship
sources.note: Native-centered kinship resource on tiyospaye, extended care, cradleboards, family work, camp circles, and later documented tipis.

sources.title: Oceti Sakowin Nation
sources.note: Native Knowledge 360 account of Seven Council Fires groups, present nations, self-government, responsibilities, and storytelling.

sources.title: Land and Lifeways
sources.note: Minnesota Historical Society account of Eastern Dakota seasonal movement, hunting, fishing, crops, rice, maple sugar, hides, and communal support.

sources.title: Mni Sota Wakpa Stories and Reflections
sources.note: Dakota voices on fish preservation, wild rice, maple sugar, community sharing, waterways, and land relationships.

sources.title: Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community history
sources.note: Community account of deep Minnesota homelands, river and lake subsistence, villages, persistence, and present language teaching.

sources.title: Whitecap Dakota Nation history
sources.note: Dakota Nation account naming Oceti Sakowin as an alliance of Dakota, Lakota, and Nakota groups and stressing living continuity.

sources.title: Dakota Wicohan
sources.note: Dakota-led language and lifeways organization emphasizing elder voices, arts, language, and intergenerational transmission.

sources.title: Dakota Values
sources.note: Dakota Wicohan curriculum on kinship, language, relatives, introductions, values, and community relationships.

sources.title: Culture: Mni Wakan Oyate
sources.note: State and tribal teaching resource on kinship, elders, children, learning, roles, songs, ceremony, and later documented social life.

sources.title: Plants Along the Santa Fe Trail
sources.note: National Park Service account of prairie turnip as a documented staple among several Plains peoples including Lakota.

sources.title: Native Plant Garden
sources.note: Tribally consulted NPS resource on later documented Lakota and Dakota food, medicine, cleansing, and plant knowledge.

sources.title: Indigenous Fire Practices Shape Our Land
sources.note: NPS account of later documented Lakota burning for camp safety, grazing, and medicinal plants.

sources.title: American Licorice
sources.note: US Forest Service review of later recorded Lakota uses for fever, earache, toothache, and sore throat.

sources.title: Quarry History
sources.note: NPS account of 3,000 years of quarrying, many nations, pipe uses, and later Dakota presence.

sources.title: Quarrying: The Unbroken Legacy
sources.note: NPS account of demanding quarry work, craft, exchange, many participating peoples, and living continuation.

sources.title: Affiliated Tribal Nations
sources.note: NPS consultation page recognizing twenty-three affiliated tribal nations and the quarry as a sacred gathering place.

sources.title: Battiste Good Lakota Winter Counts
sources.note: US Interior resource identifying winter counts as pictorial historical records and dating the surviving object and shown glyphs much later.

sources.title: Reverend Stephen and Mary Riggs
sources.note: Minnesota Historical Society account dating the first alphabet and grammar work to the 1830s with Dakota collaborators.

sources.title: The Word Carrier of Santee Normal Training School
sources.note: Minnesota Historical Society account of the Dakota-language newspaper from 1871 and its translation and colonial education context.

sources.title: Living Traditions: Dakota, Nakota, Lakota Life
sources.note: South Dakota museum education booklet on Seven Council Fires naming, languages, regional change, homes, food, and arts.
